// Expected values for the stonecutter's work (docs/rules/stonecutting.md), captured from the original program in the emulator
// (ADR 0008): tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb goods with a finished stonecutter's building (type 4) at a flag, reduced to the
// passes that matter. A scenario starts with a "#" line that names its verb command; each line after it gives, for a pass, the 16
// bytes of the castle's stonecutter (slot 12, s12=) where his node, state, or part of the cut changed (and at a checkpoint), the
// 18 bytes of the building (b=) where they changed, the object bytes that changed (o=x,y:old>new;...), the flag's byte 4 and goods
// bytes (g=) where they changed, and the generator's words (rng=) as they stand. A heap's object code goes up by one at each cut
// (0x48 to 0x4f) and is 0 after the last. Not production code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the
// program produced.
